prompt: The client asks: "Should we offer a 20% discount for paying a year up front?" Fact sheet: the monthly plan is $50; the average monthly customer stays 9 months; the annual plan at 20% off would be $480; 40% of surveyed customers would choose the annual plan; the company is opening an office in Austin. Which is the best recommendation?

options.text: An annual customer pays $480 up front, more than the $450 the average monthly customer pays over 9 months, and 40% of customers say they would switch. The main risk is that loyal customers who would have paid $600 over a year switch to $480. Putting it together, offer the annual plan at 20% off.
options.feedback: The answer comes last. Lead with the recommendation, then support it.

options.text: On one hand, an annual customer pays $480 up front, more than the $450 the average monthly customer pays over 9 months, and 40% of customers say they would switch. It depends on the client's priorities, so I'd want more analysis before committing either way.

options.text: Offer the annual plan at 20% off. The company is opening an office in Austin. An annual customer pays $480 up front, more than the $450 the average monthly customer pays over 9 months, and 40% of customers say they would switch.
